name: Hierarchical Implicit Grids (HIGS)
definition: A method for spatial scene understanding that captures geometric (SDF) and semantic (vision-language) information using hierarchical implicit grids. It solves two tasks: SDF estimation for scene construction and open-vocabulary object grounding. It aligns submaps directly in feature space via hierarchical optimization, avoiding explicit geometric reconstruction.
summary: Hierarchical Implicit Grids is a spatial scene understanding method that captures geometric and semantic data using multiresolution grids, distinguished by its tailored dense and sparse indexing strategies and fixed decoder to prevent catastrophic forgetting.
